classification.difficultyReason: Model two purchase totals with simultaneous linear equations and solve by routine elimination.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming a pair of simultaneous equations.

Six model horses and 7 model cows can be bought for $\$250$. Thirteen model cows and 11 model horses can be bought for $\$460$. What is the cost of each model animal?

answer.worked:
Let $h$ and $c$ be the costs, in dollars, of one model horse and one model cow respectively.
$$\begin{align*}6h+7c&=250 &&\text{(1)}\\11h+13c&=460 &&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$
Multiply equation (1) by 13 and equation (2) by 7:
$$\begin{align*}78h+91c&=3250 &&\text{(3)}\\77h+91c&=3220 &&\text{(4)}\end{align*}$$
Subtract equation (4) from equation (3):
$$\begin{align*}(78h+91c)-(77h+91c)&=3250-3220\\h&=30\end{align*}$$
Substitute $h=30$ into equation (1):
$$\begin{align*}6(30)+7c&=250\\180+7c&=250\\7c&=70\\c&=10\end{align*}$$
Check both purchases:
$$\begin{align*}6(30)+7(10)&=250\\11(30)+13(10)&=460\end{align*}$$
Each model horse costs $\$30.00$ and each model cow costs $\$10.00$.
